title: The rocket that destroyed itself because of one number
hook: A rocket blew itself up because one number was too big.
summary: In 1996 Europe's first Ariane 5 rocket destroyed itself 37 seconds after launch because old Ariane 4 software could not hold a larger number.
sources: ESA/CNES Ariane 501 Inquiry Board report (1996): first flight 4 June 1996, failure about 37 seconds after lift-off, 64-bit float to 16-bit integer overflow in inertial reference system reused from Ariane 4, backup ran identical software
Encyclopaedia Britannica / Wikipedia 'Ariane flight V88': Kourou, French Guiana, Cluster satellites lost, no injuries, about ten years of development

lines.text: A rocket blew itself up because one number was too big.
In nineteen ninety-six, Europe's Ariane Five made its first launch.
It reused trusted software from the older Ariane Four.
But it flew faster, so one number grew too large.
lines.caps: But it *flew faster, | one *number | grew too *large

lines.text: The computer had no room for it.
The guidance system failed, and the identical backup failed too.
Thirty-seven seconds up, the rocket turned, broke apart, and destroyed itself.
Nobody was hurt, but the satellites were lost.
Ten years of work, undone by one number.

post.caption:
Ten years of work, lost in thirty-seven seconds. Nobody was hurt, but one tiny number did it all.
Have you ever had a small bug ruin a big plan?
